nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words and let $\bar y$ be the bitwise complement of $y$. Adding $x$ and $\bar y$ with carry in $1$ gives the $n$-bit result $x - y$ (the difference modulo $2^n$), and the carry out is $1$ exactly when there is no unsigned borrow, that is, when $y \le x$ as unsigned integers.
nodes.title: Subtraction by addition

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words, let $\bar y$ be the bitwise complement of $y$, and let $K$ satisfy $n \le 2^K$. Evaluate the $n$-bit carry-lookahead adder with $K$ levels, with XOR, AND and OR gates, on the bits of $x$, the bits of $\bar y$ and carry in $1$. Then for every $i < n$, output $i$ is bit $i$ (counting from the least significant bit $0$) of $x - y$ modulo $2^n$.
nodes.title: The carry-lookahead adder subtracts

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words and let $c$ be a carry-in bit. Evaluate the $n$-bit overflow adder and the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder, with XOR, AND and OR gates, on the bits of $x$, the bits of $y$ and $c$. Then for every $o < n + 1$, output $o$ of the overflow adder equals output $o$ of the ripple-carry adder: the first $n + 1$ outputs (the $n$ sum bits and the carry out) agree.
nodes.title: The overflow adder extends the ripple-carry adder

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words. Evaluate the $n$-bit overflow adder, with XOR, AND and OR gates, on the bits of $x$, the bits of $y$ and carry in $0$. Its last output (output $n + 1$) is $1$ exactly when the two's complement addition $x + y$ overflows, that is, when the sum of the two's complement values of $x$ and $y$ is at least $2^{n-1}$ or less than $-2^{n-1}$.
nodes.title: The overflow flag

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words. Evaluate the $n$-bit overflow adder, with XOR, AND and OR gates, on the bits of $x$, the bits of $y$ and carry in $0$. Then for every $i < n$, output $i$ is bit $i$ (counting from the least significant bit $0$) of $x + y$ modulo $2^n$.
nodes.title: Sum bits of the overflow adder

nodes.summary: The $n$-bit overflow adder is the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder with one extra XOR gate. It has the same $2n + 1$ inputs (the bits of the two summands, then the carry in) and $5n + 1$ gates: the $5n$ gates of the ripple-carry adder, followed by an XOR of the carry into bit $n - 1$ and the carry into bit $n$ (the carry out). Here the carry into bit $0$ is the carry in, and for $n = 0$ the index $n - 1$ is read as $0$.…
nodes.title: The overflow adder

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words and let $\bar y$ be the bitwise complement of $y$. Evaluate the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder, with XOR, AND and OR gates, on the bits of $x$, the bits of $\bar y$ and carry in $1$. Its carry out (output $n$) is $1$ exactly when there is no unsigned borrow in $x - y$, that is, when $y \le x$ as unsigned integers.
nodes.title: Carry out of ripple-carry subtraction

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words and let $\bar y$ be the bitwise complement of $y$. Evaluate the $n$-bit ripple-carry adder, with XOR, AND and OR gates, on the bits of $x$, the bits of $\bar y$ and carry in $1$. Then for every $i < n$, output $i$ is bit $i$ (counting from the least significant bit $0$) of $x - y$ modulo $2^n$.
nodes.title: The ripple-carry adder subtracts

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $x$ and $y$ be $n$-bit words. The two's complement addition $x + y$ overflows (the sum of the two's complement values of $x$ and $y$ is at least $2^{n-1}$ or less than $-2^{n-1}$) exactly when the carry into the sign bit $n - 1$ differs from the carry out of it, both carries taken when adding $x$ and $y$ with carry in $0$.
nodes.title: Signed overflow is the XOR of the last two carries

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
